home.odor.title: Predicting Smell from Molecular Structure
home.odor.desc: A graph neural network that predicts odor descriptors of flavor molecules, running entirely in your browser.
home.fi.title: Improving Dairy Flavor with Bayesian Optimization
home.fi.desc: Choose a dairy product and a direction to see how Bayesian optimization decides which flavor compounds to add and how much. You can also import your own GC-MS results, compare a sample with a target (e.g. formula and human milk) by OAV or ROAV and odor profile, and get directions for what to add; your data stay in your browser.

home.kb.title: Flavor Knowledge Base
home.kb.desc: Look up key odorants, detection data and related papers by food or flavor compound, and analyze paper abstracts by DOI.
home.taste.title: Predicting Taste from Molecular Structure
home.taste.desc: A graph neural network that predicts whether a small molecule is sweet, bitter, umami or tasteless, with dairy-related examples, running in your browser.
lit.food_placeholder: e.g. yogurt; leave empty for any food
contrib.title: Which atoms drive the "{label}" prediction
contrib.none: Removing any single atom changes this probability by less than 0.5 percentage points, so no atom is colored.
contrib.note: Orange atoms raise the probability, blue atoms lower it. This shows what the model relies on, not a proven structure-activity cause.
home.gcms.title: GC-MS Flavor Interpreter
home.gcms.privacy: Your data never leaves your computer: all analysis runs in your browser, even offline
home.gcms.desc: Upload one sample's GC-MS peak table and your standard file: the page recognizes different instrument formats, unifies compound names and CAS numbers, matches targets by explicit rules, then computes OAV or ROAV, ranks key aroma compounds and draws a flavor profile.
footer.odor_model: Odor model: odor predictions on this page come from the graph neural network of this site's odor predictor, trained on data from The Good Scents Company and Leffingwell & Associates (Sanchez-Lengeling et al., 2019, arXiv:1910.10685, CC BY-NC), curated and merged by OpenPOM (Barsainyan et al., 2023); the raw data and odor labels are not redistributed here. The model and its predictions are for non-commercial academic demonstration only.
wf.intro: Five projects form one flavor development workflow:
wf.1.title: Predict a molecule's odor
wf.2.title: Browse the odor space
wf.2.desc: See how thousands of molecules relate on an odor map
wf.3.title: Find ingredients / substitutes
wf.3.desc: Search by target flavor, or find molecules that smell alike
wf.4.title: Improve a formulation
wf.4.desc: Bayesian optimization suggests which flavor compounds to add
home.finder.title: Flavor Ingredient Finder
home.finder.desc: Two everyday flavorist tasks: search more than 5,000 molecules for a target flavor (such as creamy or coconut), or find substitutes that smell similar but differ in structure.
home.finder.tags: Graph neural network · Odor similarity · Substitutes
wf.5.title: Interpret GC-MS results
wf.5.desc: Turn instrument data into key aroma compounds and a flavor profile
home.map.title: Odor Space Map
home.map.desc: More than 5,000 flavor molecules drawn as a zoomable map by AI-predicted odor, so molecules that smell alike sit together; switch to a map arranged by molecular structure to compare, and highlight the key aroma compounds of a food.
home.map.tags: UMAP · Graph neural network · Odor vs structure
home.perc.title: Why People Smell Differently
home.perc.desc: Public smell ratings of 480 molecules by 55 people: how much of the differences comes from the molecule, personal taste or noise; whether a new consumer's preferences can be predicted from a few ratings; and whether consumer segments exist. Labels are standardized and the data quality-checked first.
home.perc.tags: Variance decomposition · Personalized prediction · Data quality
